Remembrance adorns the tongue, and reflection adorns the heart. Each thing has its own ornament. The ornament of the soul is good practice joined to struggle. The ornament of the heart is unbroken union in the moment of contemplation. The ornament of the secret core is the realities of nearness in the field of face-to-face vision.

When the Exalted Lord asks, "Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah?", He hints that these adornments are not held back from those who seek them, or from people whose hearts are present. The storehouse of blessings is full, and all it lacks is seekers. The table of kindness and mercy is laid and waits only for guests.

The master of the spiritual path (ṭarīqah) said in his whispered prayer: "Seekers, hurry, for the treasure is near! Night travellers, do not sleep, for the morning is near! You who hasten, rejoice, for the dwelling is near! Thirsty ones, be patient, for the spring is near! Strangers, be glad, for the generous host is near! Seekers of the Friend, take heart, for the answer is near!" And: "O Opener of my heart! What harm would it do if You opened my heart and laid Your balm on my spirit? How can I look for profit when my hands hold no capital? What if, out of Your bounty, You cast me into good fortune?"

### In short

- Only Allah, the Creator, decides what is lawful. Forbidding the good clothes and food He allowed is a sin, not piety.
- Wearing good clothes when one has the means is gratitude, so long as there is no showing off or pride. The simple dress of early leaders came from generosity and from their role as leaders.
- The Sunnah is to use gratefully what is at hand, neither chasing luxury nor spoiling what is good.
- The world's good things belong by right to the believers though others share them now. In the Hereafter they will be the believers' alone, pure and lasting.

33.text:
Having rebuked those who forbade what Allah allowed, the surah now lists what He has truly forbidden: "Say, “My Lord has only forbidden open and secret indecencies, sinfulness, unjust aggression, associating ˹others˺ with Allah ˹in worship˺—a practice He has never authorized—and attributing to Allah what you do not know.”" It is by leaving these things that His pleasure is won. The idolaters were lost in a twofold ignorance. They denied themselves, for no reason, the good things Allah had made lawful. At the same time they eagerly embraced what was truly forbidden, which would bring Allah's anger and the punishment of the Hereafter. So they were doubly deprived: of the blessings of this world, and of the blessings they might have had in the next.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, “My Lord has only forbidden open and secret indecencies"**: the fawāḥish are grave sins such as fornication, both the open kind and the hidden kind. One explanation gives open adultery and the taking of secret lovers as examples. Imam Aḥmad recorded from ʿAbdullāh that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that no one is more protective of honour than Allah, and that is why He forbade indecencies, open and secret. He added that no one loves praise more than Allah. The hadith is also in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs. The open and hidden fāḥishah was explained under Sūrat al-Anʿām.

**"sinfulness"**: the word is ithm. As-Suddī said al-ithm means disobedience, and Mujāhid said it covers every kind of disobedience. One explanation takes it as intoxicants and quotes a poet: "I sipped sin until my mind went astray. Thus indeed does sin take away minds."

**"unjust aggression"**: baghy. As-Suddī said it is transgressing against people without any justification. Others call it unlawful high-handedness, or oppressing people in their persons, their wealth or their honour. Mujāhid said that the oppressor commits oppression against himself. So ithm is the sin a person commits against himself, while baghy is transgression against others, and Allah has forbidden both. Put another way, ithm covers the sins whose harm falls on oneself, and baghy covers the sins that touch other people's rights and dealings.

**"associating ˹others˺ with Allah ˹in worship˺"**: this forbids shirk, calling on partners besides Allah and worshipping others alongside Him.

**"a practice He has never authorized"**: no warrant was ever sent down for it, no scripture, no proof and no decisive evidence.

**"and attributing to Allah what you do not know.”"** This means lies and inventions, such as the claim that Allah has a son, and the other false creeds of which the idolaters had no knowledge. It includes forbidding crops and cattle, good things and clothing, which He never forbade. It also covers speaking about Allah without knowledge concerning His names, attributes, actions and sacred law. A similar verse says, "So shun the impurity of idolatry, and shun words of falsehood" (22:30).

### Why does the list name these sins in particular?

The list covers almost every kind of prohibition and sin. It takes in matters of belief and of conduct, sins against oneself, and the seizing of other people's rights. Shirk and lying about Allah are, plainly, grave sins. The list was also chosen because the people of the Jāhiliyyah were caught up in every one of these crimes. It exposed one more side of their ignorance: they kept away from what was lawful for them and did not hesitate to take what was forbidden.

### Where does excess in religion lead?

Some Arab tribes circled the Kaʿbah completely bare, thinking it brought them closer to Allah. In the pre-Islamic period they also gave up certain things, such as goat's milk or meat, when setting out on Hajj, imagining they were doing great acts of piety. People of every age have fallen into this kind of misguided action. They do not bring the demands of religion into their everyday lives. Only on certain occasions do they make a great show of religion, by paying special attention to some pointless act. Then they claim that by attending to trifles they are doing Allah's will to the fullest.

A sad but certain result of excess (ghuluww) in religion and of invented practices (bidʿah) is that those caught up in them grow used to neglecting the root of religion and its real demands. So the ḥarām that comes from excess and innovation is twofold. Getting involved in them is a sin in itself. Far graver, by comparison, is being cut off from Allah's true religion and from the genuine way of the Prophet ﷺ. We seek refuge with Allah from such a fate.

### What does Allah want instead?

Allah wants a person to keep from being wasteful, which means not overstepping the limits He has set.

- He should not treat the permitted as forbidden, or the forbidden as permitted.
- He should avoid shameful acts, and whatever common sense shows to be plainly evil, and shun every kind of excess.
- Whenever the truth comes before him, he should accept it and let everything else go.
- He should cleanse himself completely of shirk. He should give no one the exalted bond that is the right of the one God alone.
- He should not choose a path for himself and then ascribe it to Allah without reason. He should remain always Allah's servant and adopt no way unfit for a servant.

### In short

- Allah has forbidden only real evils: indecencies open and hidden, sin against oneself, aggression against others, shirk, and speaking about Him without knowledge.
- The idolaters were doubly deprived. They forbade themselves lawful blessings while embracing the true prohibitions.
- Excess and invented practices are sins in themselves, and they lead people away from the essentials of religion.
- What Allah wants is a servant who keeps His limits, accepts the truth and attributes nothing to Him without knowledge.

34.text:
The previous verses exposed two crimes of the disbelievers: they treated the ḥalāl as ḥarām, and made the ḥarām ḥalāl for themselves on their own authority. Now comes a reminder of where such conduct ends: "For each community there is an appointed term. When their time arrives, they can neither delay it for a moment, nor could they advance it". Wrongdoers who are still enjoying Allah's blessings, and seem nowhere near punishment, should not forget how Allah deals with people.

### Phrase by phrase

**"For each community there is an appointed term."** Each ummah, meaning each generation and nation, has a fixed and limited span. One explanation says every people with a religion has a time appointed for its destruction.

**"When their time arrives"**: the term they were destined for, the time of their destruction.

**"they can neither delay it for a moment"**: they are not granted a fraction of a second beyond it.

**"nor could they advance it"**: nor are they destroyed before their time, even by a fraction of a second.

### Why do wrongdoers seem to escape?

Allah's customary way, out of His boundless mercy, is to give sinners a long rope, in the hope that they will somehow stop what they are doing. But the length of that rope and the time of that respite are fixed in Allah's perfect knowledge. When the time comes, it simply comes, neither late nor early, and the guilty are seized by punishment. Sometimes the punishment falls in this world. If it does not, it waits for them soon after death.

### Why mention "advance" at all?

Saying the term is neither late nor early is a turn of speech. It is like asking a shopkeeper, "What is your last price, more or less?" Plainly the question is about the lower price, and "more" is added only as a tag. In the same way, the real point here is that there will be no delay once the appointed time comes. Mentioning "before" alongside "late" simply brings the statement closer to ordinary ways of speaking.

### How is a nation's term decided?

In Allah's plan of creation, each individual has the chance to do well or badly in this world until his period of trial is over. For a community or nation, Allah's decision is not held back to such a limit. It is made on the basis of how that community responds once the truth has been put before it. When a community's time is up, it is sometimes destroyed by an extraordinary punishment. At other times it is punished by being removed from its position of honour and supremacy.

### In short

- Every nation has a term fixed in Allah's knowledge, and it cannot be put off or brought forward by a moment.
- Allah gives wrongdoers a long rope out of mercy, but when their time comes punishment falls, in this world or after death.
- A nation's fate turns on how it responds once the truth has been presented to it.

35.text:
Allah again addresses all humanity, with good news and a warning: "O children of Adam! When messengers from among yourselves come to you reciting My revelations—whoever shuns evil and mends their ways, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve". He sent them messengers who conveyed His signs, and the response to those messengers decides each person's end.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O children of Adam! When messengers from among yourselves come to you"**: messengers of your own kind, human beings like you, sent to you from Allah. In the Arabic, the word for "when" is immā, in which the nūn of the conditional particle in has merged with an extra mā.

**"reciting My revelations"**: reciting what Allah revealed to them of His scripture, and explaining His commands and prohibitions. Then follow them and what they bring.

**"whoever shuns evil"**: whoever has taqwā. That means leaving the forbidden and doing acts of obedience, following Allah's instructions and keeping away from what He has not allowed. Others explain it as believing in the scripture and the messenger, or as fearing to associate anything with Allah.

**"and mends their ways"**: sets right their deeds, and what lies between them and their Lord.

**"there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve"**: on the Day of Judgement they will have no fear of punishment. They will not grieve over missing Paradise, or over the pleasures of this world that passed them by.

### What decides a person's final home?

Whether a person's final home is Heaven or Hell is decided by how he responds once the truth has appeared before him. The truth must come with arguments whose soundness his own reason confirms. That is what it means for the message to be conveyed in the full sense. Allah sends messengers from among people themselves, so that this can happen.

### In short

- Allah sent humanity messengers of their own kind, reciting His revelations and explaining His commands and prohibitions.
- Those who respond with taqwā, leaving the forbidden and setting their deeds right, will have no fear or grief in the Hereafter.
- A person's final home depends on his response once the truth has reached him with clear arguments.

36.text:
The other side of the choice follows: "But those who receive Our revelations with denial and arrogance will be the residents of the Fire. They will be there forever". Their hearts rejected Allah's signs, and they were too proud to live by them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"But those who receive Our revelations with denial"**: those who deny Allah's signs, His scripture and His messenger, and reject them in their hearts.

**"and arrogance"**: too proud to believe in them, or to act on what their messengers brought.

**"will be the residents of the Fire."** They are its rightful companions.

**"They will be there forever"**: with no end to their stay, never dying there and never being taken out.

### Why does arrogance lead to the Fire?

If a person still refuses the truth after it has been fully conveyed to him, he does so out of egotism. His wish to keep his own superiority stops him from humbling himself before the truth. For such a person, before Allah, there is no fate but Hell.

### In short

- Those who deny Allah's revelations and are too proud to follow them will live in the Fire forever.
- Refusing the truth after it is clearly conveyed comes from ego, the wish to stay above it rather than bow to it.

37.text:
The surah now turns to the worst of wrongdoers and their end: "Who does more wrong than those who fabricate lies against Allah or deny His revelations? They will receive what is destined for them, until Our messenger-angels arrive to take their souls, asking them, “Where are those ˹false gods˺ you used to invoke besides Allah?” They will cry, “They have failed us,” and they will confess against themselves that they were indeed disbelievers". No one is more unjust than such people, yet they still receive their share of this life until death comes for them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Who does more wrong than those who fabricate lies against Allah"**: none is more unjust, more insolent or bolder toward Allah, than one who invents a lie about Him. He may ascribe to Allah a partner or a child, or call Him deficient in some way. Or he may claim Allah said something He never said.

**"or deny His revelations?"** Or he rejects the signs Allah revealed, meaning the Qur'an and Muhammad ﷺ, the clear signs that guide to the right way of life.

**"They will receive what is destined for them"**: literally "their portion from the Book". Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī said it means each person's deeds, provision and lifespan. Ar-Rabīʿ ibn Anas and ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said much the same. Another explanation says it is their lot inscribed in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawḥ al-maḥfūẓ): provision, length of life and other matters. Others say it is their destined share of worldly pleasure. One explanation takes it as what they were promised in the Book, such as their faces turned black and their eyes blue.

Two other verses make the same point:

> "Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will never succeed.” ˹It is only˺ a brief enjoyment in this world, then to Us is their return, then We will make them taste the severe punishment for their disbelief" (10:69-70).

> "But whoever disbelieves, do not let their disbelief grieve you ˹O Prophet˺. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of all they did. Surely Allah knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart. We allow them enjoyment for a little while, then ˹in time˺ We will force them into a harsh torment" (31:23-24).

**"until Our messenger-angels arrive to take their souls"**: the angel of death and his helpers. In effect: give them respite, O Muhammad, until then.

**"asking them, “Where are those ˹false gods˺ you used to invoke besides Allah?”"** When death comes to the idolaters, the angels take their souls toward the Fire and terrify them with a reproach. Where are the so-called partners you called on and worshipped in the world instead of Allah? Call them now, if they can help you, and let them save you from what you are suffering.

**"They will cry, “They have failed us,”"**: literally "they have gone astray from us". They have vanished and left us, and we no longer see them, so we hope for nothing from them. One explanation says the false gods are too busy with themselves to pay any attention to their worshippers. Others render it: the gods we worshipped are gone, and we do not know where.

**"and they will confess against themselves that they were indeed disbelievers"**: at death they admit and declare against themselves that they disbelieved in Allah and the messengers in the life of this world. But a confession made then will only stand as proof against them, and it will not help them.

### What does a denier lean on?

Whenever a person rejects the truth, he imagines he has something to back him. Some lean on money and influence, others on standing and popularity. He may feel sure that his affairs are so well arranged that turning down the truth cannot harm him. He may pride himself on a clever mind that can find fine words to present his own ideas as if they came straight from Allah.

All of these are grave mistakes. He has taken as props for his salvation the very things given to him as his test. On the Day of Judgement, when all these false props abandon him, he will easily see the truth. He rejected the truth out of plain ignorance, though he kept quoting "principles" to justify himself.

### In short

- No one does greater wrong than one who lies about Allah, by ascribing partners, faults or words to Him, or who rejects His revelations.
- Such people still receive their written share of provision and life, but only for a brief enjoyment.
- At death the angels mock them by asking where their false gods are, and they admit they were disbelievers, too late to help them.
- Wealth, status and clever words are a test, not a support, and they will desert the denier when he needs them.

38.text:
The scene moves to the Hereafter, where those who joined partners with Allah, lied about Him and rejected His signs are sent into the Fire: "Allah will say, “Enter the Fire along with the ˹evil˺ groups of jinn and humans that preceded you.” Whenever a group enters Hell, it will curse the preceding one until they are all gathered inside, the followers will say about their leaders, “Our Lord! They have misled us, so multiply their torment in the Fire.” He will answer, “It has already been multiplied for all, but you do not know.”" Those who once stood together now turn on one another.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Allah will say, “Enter the Fire along with the ˹evil˺ groups of jinn and humans that preceded you.”"** On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will tell them to enter among the nations who were like them in conduct. These are the disbelieving nations of jinn and humans who went before them in disbelief and error. One explanation has the angels saying it to them. In the Arabic, "into the Fire" is tied to the verb "enter".

**"Whenever a group enters Hell, it will curse the preceding one"**: each nation, the followers of each religion, will curse its "sister" nation that went in before it, because it went astray on that nation's account. One explanation takes the group (ummah) here as the leaders who mislead, and its "sister" (ukht) as the misled public. Allah's Friend (al-Khalīl), Ibrāhīm (Abraham), warned his people of this: "But on the Day of Judgment you will disown and curse one another. Your home will be the Fire, and you will have no helper!" (29:25). Allah also says:

> "˹Consider the Day˺ when those who misled others will disown their followers—when they face the torment—and the bonds that united them will be cut off. The ˹misled˺ followers will cry, “If only we could have a second chance, we would disown them as they disowned us.” And so Allah will make them remorseful of their misdeeds. And they will never ˹be able to˺ leave the Fire" (2:166-167).

**"until they are all gathered inside"**: until every group, from the first to the last, has caught up with the others and they are gathered together in the Fire.

**"the followers will say about their leaders"**: literally "the last of them will say about the first of them". The followers, the lowly ones who entered last, will speak about the earlier nations, their leaders and masters whom they revered and followed. The earlier nations were greater criminals than those who followed them, which is why they entered the Fire first. So the followers will complain about them to Allah, since it was they who misled them from the right path.

**"“Our Lord! They have misled us, so multiply their torment in the Fire.”"** These led us astray from Your religion and from obeying You, and made the path of error look beautiful to us. So give them double what You inflict on us. Another verse records the same plea:

> "On the Day their faces are ˹constantly˺ flipped in the Fire, they will cry, “Oh! If only we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!” And they will say, “Our Lord! We obeyed our leaders and elite, but they led us astray from the ˹Right˺ Way. Our Lord! Give them double ˹our˺ punishment, and condemn them tremendously.”" (33:66-68).

**"He will answer, “It has already been multiplied for all"**: each group, of you and of them, will have a double share. In effect: We have done what you asked, and repaid each according to their deeds. Allah says elsewhere, "For those who disbelieve and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, We will add more punishment to their punishment" (16:88). He also says, "Yet they will certainly ˹be made to˺ carry their own burdens, as well as other burdens along with their own" (29:13). And: "as well as some of the burdens of those they mislead without knowledge" (16:25).

**"but you do not know.”"** You cannot perceive it, because of the severity of the torment. The verb may also be read yaʿlamūn, "they do not know", meaning that no party knows what the other is suffering.

### Why will each feel their own pain is the worst?

This verse shows a scene full of lessons. When misguiding leaders and their misled public are thrown into Hell together, every false veil will fall from their eyes, and everyone will be seen as he truly is. The followers will ask Allah to give their leaders double their own punishment. The answer will be that the leaders are already receiving double, but the followers do not know it. In Hell, whatever punishment anyone receives will feel so severe that he will think no one else suffers such agony. Each will feel himself the most afflicted of all.

### In short

- On the Day of Resurrection the deniers will enter the Fire with the earlier nations of jinn and humans who were like them.
- Each nation will curse the one before it, and followers will disown the leaders they once revered.
- The followers will ask double punishment for their leaders, but every group's torment is already multiplied.
- In Hell each person will feel his own suffering to be the worst, unaware of the others' pain.

39.text:
The leaders answer their followers: "Then the leaders will say to their followers, “You were no better than us! So taste the torment for what you used to commit.”" Those who once flattered one another now try to push one another toward the worst fate.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Then the leaders will say to their followers"**: literally "the first of them will say to the last of them", the nations who were followed speaking to those who followed them.

**"“You were no better than us!"** You have no advantage over us that would make our punishment double yours. As-Suddī explained it as: you were led astray just as we were led astray. You disbelieved as we disbelieved, and worshipped others besides Allah as we did. You did not disbelieve because of us, so you and we are equal in this plight. You have no claim on us that would earn you a lighter punishment. What you suffer is the result of your own actions, and you have no excuse for following falsehood.

**"So taste the torment for what you used to commit.”"** One explanation puts these words in Allah's mouth, and another in the leaders'. Taste the punishment, as we taste it, for the idolatry, disbelief and disobedience that you said and did in the life of this world.

### How do the leaders defend themselves?

In this world, such leaders and their followers posed as each other's well-wishers, ready to make sacrifices for one another. The leaders humoured every wish of the public, and the public made heroes of their leaders. In the Fire, the followers will turn on them: "Curse you! What a dreadful leadership you gave us, showing us false sights and then hurling us into this terrible torment!"

The leaders will reply: "You wanted a religion to your own taste. When you found one with us, you rushed to us. In that same age there were servants of Allah calling you to the path of real success. You heard their call and paid it no attention." They will add: "You are no better than us. We set up our leadership to serve our desires, and you followed us to serve yours. So in truth we stand in the same place, and here you must take the same punishment our deeds have earned."

The idolaters will argue in the same way at the gathering of the Resurrection, as another passage describes:

> "The arrogant will respond to the lowly, “Did we ever hinder you from guidance after it came to you? In fact, you were wicked ˹on your own˺.” The lowly will say to the arrogant, “No! It was your plotting by day and night—when you ordered us to disbelieve in Allah and to set up equals with Him.” They will ˹all˺ hide ˹their˺ remorse when they see the torment. And We will put shackles around the necks of the disbelievers. Will they be rewarded except for what they used to do" (34:32-33).

### What becomes of bonds built on self-interest?

In this world, self-interested leaders and self-interested followers are tied by strong bonds of friendship. Each side speaks well of the other and finds kind words for it. In the Hereafter each group will hate the other, and each will try to push the other toward the worst of fates.

### In short

- The misleading leaders will tell their followers that they were no better, for both chose disbelief.
- The followers cannot shift their guilt onto their leaders, since each followed falsehood by choice.
- Friendships built on shared desires and self-interest turn into hatred and blame in the Hereafter.

40.text:
The earlier verses spoke of messengers coming to every people. They are understood as a covenant that each person made before birth, in the world of spirits. When Allah's prophets came with guidance, people would listen in earnest and act on it. Those who kept the pledge would be saved from sorrow and earn lasting peace, and those who denied the prophets would face the endless punishment of Jahannam. Now the surah shows what happened when people came into the world. Some threw the pledge behind their backs, and others held to it and did good. Verses 40 and 41 describe the deniers, and verses 42 and 43 the believers who kept faith: "Surely those who receive our revelations with denial and arrogance, the gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle. This is how We reward the wicked".

### Phrase by phrase

**"Surely those who receive our revelations with denial and arrogance"**: those who reject Allah's clear signs and verses, Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur'an. They are too proud to believe in them or follow them, and so they have lost everything.

**"the gates of heaven will not be opened for them"**: this has two explanations, given in the sections below. Their deeds and their supplication will not rise through those gates, and their souls will not be let in.

**"nor will they enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle."** The verb yalij comes from wulūj, entering a narrow opening. Jamal is a camel, and samm the eye of a needle. Ibn Masʿūd said the word means a male camel born of a she-camel, and another narration calls it the she-camel's mate. The camel is one of the largest animals and the eye of a needle one of the smallest openings. Its passing through is impossible in practice, and so is their entry into Paradise. The point is that their punishment in Hell is everlasting.

Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah reported that Ibn ʿAbbās used to recite the word as jummal, a thick rope. On that reading, Paradise stays closed to them until a rope can be threaded through a needle.

**"This is how We reward the wicked"**: so Allah repays those who sin through disbelief, the idolaters, and all who stubbornly do wrong.

### What does "the gates of heaven will not be opened" mean?

One explanation is that their good deeds and supplication will not rise through those gates. Mujāhid and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said this, as did Ibn ʿAbbās in the reports of al-ʿAwfī and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah. ʿAṭāʾ also reported it from Ibn ʿAbbās. Al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ records from Ibn ʿAbbās that the gates will be opened neither for them nor for their prayers. Their prayers will not be answered. Their deeds will be kept from reaching the place where the deeds of Allah's righteous servants are stored, which the Qur'an calls ʿIlliyyīn (83:18-21, in Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn). Another verse touches on the same theme: good words rise to Allah, and good deeds lift them. A person's good deeds are what carry his good words up to Allah.

The second explanation is that the gates of heaven will not be opened for the disbelievers' souls, which will be thrown down. Aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk reported this from Ibn ʿAbbās, and it is reported from other Companions too. As-Suddī and several others gave the same meaning.

Ibn Jurayj joined the two. The gates, he said, will not be opened for their deeds or for their souls. That combines both meanings, and Allah knows best.

### What happens to the soul at death?

A hadith of al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib supports the second explanation. Ibn Jarīr reported it, and Abū Dāwūd, an-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah and Imam Aḥmad recorded it in full. In summary it runs as follows.

The Prophet ﷺ went to the funeral of a man from the Anṣār. The grave was not yet ready, so he sat down in an open spot, and the Companions sat silently around him. Then he raised his head and spoke.

When death comes to a believing servant, angels with white, shining faces come down from heaven. They bring a shroud and perfume from Paradise and sit before the dying man. Then the angel of death, ʿIzrāʾīl, comes and addresses his rūḥ, his soul: "O soul at peace, come out to the forgiveness and pleasure of your Lord." The soul leaves the body smoothly, like water flowing from the mouth of an opened water-skin. The angel of death takes it in his hands and gives it to the waiting angels, who set off with it.

Each group of angels they pass asks, "Whose pure soul is this?" They answer with the most honourable names he was known by in the world: so-and-so, son of so-and-so. At the first heaven they ask for the gate to be opened, and it is opened. More angels join them at each heaven until they reach the seventh. Then Allah says, "Write My servant's record in ʿIlliyyīn, and send him back." The soul returns to the grave.

There the angels of account sit him up and ask, "Who is your Lord?" and "What is your religion?" He answers, "Allah is my Lord, and Islam is my religion." Then they ask, "Who is this man who was sent to you?" He says, "He is the Messenger of Allah." A call comes from heaven: "My servant has spoken the truth. Spread for him a carpet from Jannah, dress him in the clothing of Paradise, and open for him a door toward Jannah." Its fragrance and breeze reach him through that door. His good deeds come to him in a handsome form, to keep him company and put him at ease.

When death comes to a disbeliever and denier, angels with dark, terrifying faces come down from heaven. They carry a coarse, ragged cloth and sit before him. The angel of death pulls out his soul as a thorny branch is dragged out through wet wool wrapped around it. When the soul comes out, its stench is worse than that of a rotting carcass. The angels set off with it.

Each group of angels they meet asks, "Whose foul soul is this?" They answer with the worst names he was known by in the world: so-and-so, son of so-and-so. At the first heaven they ask for the gate to be opened, but it is not opened for him. Then the Prophet ﷺ recited, "the gates of heaven will not be opened for them". The command comes to place his record in Sijjīn, where the records of the disobedient are kept. His soul is flung down and returns to the grave.

The angels of account sit him up and ask him the same questions. To every one he can only say, "I do not know." He is given a bed from Jahannam and clothing from Jahannam. A door is opened in his grave toward Jahannam, and its heat and flames keep reaching him. His grave is made to close tight around him. We seek refuge with Allah from it.

In short, the souls of deniers and disbelievers are carried up to the gate of heaven. When it does not open, they are thrown back down. Instead of rising, they are taken down to Sijjīn. The believer's soul, by contrast, has the gates opened for it and is carried up to the seventh heaven. So the verse may also mean that the gates of heaven are shut to them at the moment of death.

### Why is arrogance so hard to cure?

Why does the ego of those addressed stop them from accepting the call to truth? The one who calls has nothing but argument to lean on, while his hearers stand on material glories. He stands on reasons, and they stand on something solid and visible. The force of argument cannot be touched or seen. That difference breeds arrogance. People come to see the caller as beneath them, and that gives them a "reason" to ignore him.

For such people, entering Allah's mercy is as impossible as a camel passing through the eye of a needle. They ignore Allah, so Allah ignores them. He showed them glimpses of Himself through the caller, appearing before them in the form of arguments. They gave those signs no weight and refused to bow before them. How can such people have any share in His bounty?

### In short

- Those who deny Allah's revelations out of arrogance will find the gates of heaven shut to their deeds, their prayers and their souls.
- At death a believer's soul is welcomed through every heaven, while a disbeliever's soul is refused at the first gate and thrown down to Sijjīn.
- They will no more enter Paradise than a camel, or a thick rope, can pass through a needle's eye, so their punishment is everlasting.
- Arrogance grows when people value visible wealth over unseen arguments, and so they dismiss the one who calls them to the truth.

41.text:
After shutting them out of Paradise, the surah describes the added severity of their punishment: "Hell will be their bed; flames will be their cover. This is how We reward the wrongdoers". Those who rejected the truth out of pride will be surrounded by Hell from below and from above.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Hell will be their bed"**: the word is mihād, a place of rest, a bed or a floor. For them it is a bed of fire. Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī explained mihād as beds.

**"flames will be their cover."** The word is ghawāsh, plural of ghāshiyah, something that covers. In the Arabic form ghawāshin, the ending makes up for a dropped letter yāʾ. Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī said it means coverings, and aḍ-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim and as-Suddī said the same. Above them will be a covering of torment, the coverings of Hell. Even the bed they rest on and the sheet over them will come from Hell. This is an everyday image used to express how extreme the punishment is.

**"This is how We reward the wrongdoers"**: so Allah repays the idolaters, who overstepped His limits by disbelieving in Him and turning away from Him.

### Why does the closing phrase change?

The previous verse, about being kept out of Paradise, ends with "This is how We reward the wicked". This verse, describing the punishment of Hell, ends with "This is how We reward the wrongdoers". The change is deliberate, because the punishment here is more severe than the deprivation described before.

### In short

- The deniers will have Hell for their bed and its fire for their covering, enclosed in punishment from below and above.
- The image of bed and sheet expresses in plain terms how complete and severe their torment will be.
- Being denied Paradise is matched by the harsher word "wrongdoers" when the punishment of Hell itself is described.

42.text:
Having described the wretched, Allah now describes the happy: "As for those who believe and do good—We never require of any soul more than what it can afford—it is they who will be the residents of Paradise. They will be there forever". Their hearts believed, and their limbs and senses did good. They stand in contrast to those who denied Allah's signs and were arrogant toward them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"As for those who believe and do good"**: those who have faith in their Lord, in Muhammad ﷺ and in the Qur'an. They do good actions between themselves and their Lord, to the best of their ability.

**"We never require of any soul more than what it can afford"**: Allah does not ask more effort of any soul than it is able to give. Grammatically this clause is a parenthesis. "Those who believe and do good" is the subject, and its predicate, "it is they who will be the residents of Paradise", follows after the interruption. The interruption itself carries the message: faith and acting on it are within everyone's reach.

**"it is they who will be the residents of Paradise."** The believers are its rightful people. They will enter it.

**"They will be there forever"**: living there for ever, never dying and never being moved out.

### Is the condition for Paradise too hard?

Belief and good deeds are the condition for entering Paradise. Yet Allah, in His mercy, added at once that He burdens no one beyond their capacity. The point is that good deeds are not so hard as to be beyond any man or woman. Across every area of life, the rulings of the Sharīʿah have been made easy and adaptable. Every injunction has its allowances and concessions, made with sickness, weakness, travel and other human needs in mind.

Al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ explains why the reassurance comes here. When people were commanded to do good deeds, they might have found the command heavy, since doing everything good and required, everywhere and in every condition, is beyond anyone's power. These words remove that worry. Allah's injunctions take account of the different stages of human life, and they suit the conditions of every situation, time and place. With so much consideration built into them, acting on them should not be hard at all.

### In short

- Those who believe in their hearts and do good with their limbs will live in Paradise forever.
- Allah never asks more of any soul than it can give, so faith and good deeds are within everyone's reach.
- The Sharīʿah is built with concessions for sickness, weakness, travel and other needs, suited to every time and place.

43.text:
Two states of the people of Paradise are described here: hearts cleansed of every grudge, and tongues full of gratitude. "We will remove whatever bitterness they had in their hearts. Rivers will flow under their feet. And they will say, “Praise be to Allah for guiding us to this. We would have never been guided if Allah had not guided us. The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth.” It will be announced to them, “This is Paradise awarded to you for what you used to do.”" Their bliss is made complete when Allah removes all hatred and resentment from their hearts.

### Phrase by phrase

**"We will remove whatever bitterness they had in their hearts."** The word is ghill: envy and hatred, resentment or enmity, any spite that existed between them during their worldly life.

**"Rivers will flow under their feet."** Beneath their palaces, dwellings and couches in the Hereafter run rivers of wine, water, honey and milk.

**"And they will say, “Praise be to Allah for guiding us to this."** They say this once they have settled in their homes. One view says it is when they reach the spring of life. All praise and thanks belong to Allah, who led them to this home. Another explanation is that He guided them to the deeds whose reward is this Paradise, and enabled them to do them.

**"We would have never been guided if Allah had not guided us."** Had Allah not enabled us, we could never have done those deeds. Another explanation is that when they see the favour Allah did them in giving them faith, they say: we would never have been guided to the religion of Islam had Allah not guided us. In the Arabic, the answer to "if not" is left unsaid, because the clause before it already implies it.

**"The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth.”"** The messengers brought a truth beyond doubt, with glad tidings, reward and favour. Their promises of good to the righteous proved true, and so did their warnings to the wrongdoers.

**"It will be announced to them, “This is Paradise awarded to you for what you used to do.”"** Literally, "you have been made to inherit it". It was given to you out of Allah's mercy, for the good you used to do and say in the world, seeking His face. The particle that introduces the announcement can be read as a softened "that", or as a particle of explanation. That reading holds in all five places here and in the four that follow.

### How will the grudges be removed?

Al-Bukhārī recorded from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ described what happens once the believers are saved from the Fire. They will be held on a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, and the wrongs they did one another in the world will be settled. Once they are cleansed and purified, they will be allowed into Paradise. The Prophet ﷺ swore that each of them would find his home in Paradise more easily than he found his home in the world.

So when the believers have crossed the Ṣirāṭ and their rescue from Jahannam is certain, they will be stopped first so that their malice can be removed. Any grudge, ill will, or burning sense of a right withheld will be settled and washed away for good. They will enter Jannah free of malice, hatred, animosity and every such sickness of the heart. One view holds that this bridge is the last stretch of the Ṣirāṭ, next to Jannah. ʿAllāmah al-Suyūṭī took the same view.

How will rights be settled there, where no one has money? A hadith in al-Bukhārī and Muslim says the payment will be made in the currency of deeds. The wronged person will be given the good deeds of the one who wronged him. If the wrongdoer's deeds run out while rights are still owed, the sins of the wronged will be loaded onto him. In another hadith, the Prophet ﷺ called a person the greatest pauper who did good deeds in the world but neglected people's rights. Through that neglect he lost all his good deeds and stood there empty-handed.

That hadith states the general rule for settling rights and avenging wrongs. It does not mean everyone must go through it. It is possible that no one will demand his due or take revenge, and the grudges will still be removed without any of that. Some narrations say that after crossing the Ṣirāṭ, people will come to a stream and drink from it, and its water will remove all malice from every heart. Imam al-Qurṭubī explained the verse "and their Lord will give them a purifying drink" (76:21) in the same way: this water of Jannah washes every grudge from the heart.

As-Suddī described it more fully. When the people of Paradise are led to it, they will find a tree near its gate with two springs flowing from beneath its trunk. They will drink from one, and all hatred will leave their hearts, for it is the drink of cleansing. They will bathe in the other, and the glow of delight will shine on their faces. After that their hair will never be untidy and they will never be soiled.

After reciting this verse, ʿAlī al-Murtaḍā once said that he hoped ʿUthmān, Ṭalḥah, az-Zubayr and he himself would be among those whose hearts are cleansed of malice before entering Paradise. In the world these noble men had disagreements that went as far as war.

### What will Paradise feel like?

In Hell, people who were friends in the world will hate and curse each other. The atmosphere of Paradise will be completely different. Every heart there will be open to every other, and springs of love and goodwill will rise from each one. For the person in Hell his past will be a bitter memory, and for the person in Paradise a sweet one.

The future life of evil people will begin with hearts that are graveyards of regret and frustration. The good will be different. Their minds will be full of the remembrance of Allah, on whom they rightly relied. They will be glad to find that the message of the bearers of truth was entirely correct. With thanks they will recognise Allah's grace in blessing them and moving them to stand with those who called them to the truth.

### Does anyone earn Paradise by deeds alone?

An-Nasāʾī and Ibn Marduwyah recorded, in Ibn Marduwyah's wording, a hadith from Abū Hurayrah. Every one of the people of Paradise will see the seat he would have had in the Fire. He will say, "Had Allah not guided me!" and it will make him grateful. Every one of the people of the Fire will see the seat he would have had in Paradise. He will say, "If only Allah had guided me!" and it will be a source of anguish to him.

That is why the believers, given seats in Paradise that would have belonged to the people of the Fire, are told they have inherited it for what they used to do. Their good deeds earned them Allah's mercy, by which they entered Paradise and took homes there in keeping with their deeds. This is the right meaning, for the Two Ṣaḥīḥs record the Prophet ﷺ saying that no one's deeds will admit him into Paradise. The Companions asked, "Not even you, Messenger of Allah?" He replied, "Not even me, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and favour."

This shows that no one reaches Jannah by personal effort alone unless Allah's grace makes it possible. Even the effort itself is not fully in a person's control. It too comes only by Allah's grace and mercy.

### Why is entering Paradise called guidance?

Imam Rāghib al-Iṣfahānī, who explained hidāyah (guidance) thoroughly as the Qur'an uses it, said that guidance is a common word with many degrees. In truth, guidance means finding the way to Allah. The degrees of nearness to Allah are many, varied and endless, and so are the degrees of guidance.

Its lowest degree is being rescued from kufr and shirk and having īmān. At that degree a person's direction turns away from the path of error and toward Allah. Then there is the distance between Allah and His servant. Covering it takes a journey, and each stage of that journey has its own degree of guidance. So guidance is a constant need. No one can ever claim to be beyond it, not even Allah's prophets and messengers.

That is why the Prophet ﷺ not only taught his community to pray "Guide us along the Straight Path" but kept making that prayer himself. The stages and ranks of nearness to Allah have no end. Entry into Paradise is called guidance in this verse because it is the final station of guidance.

### The inner reading: hearts made pure

This is the description of the noble ones of the spiritual path (ṭarīqah) and the travellers on the road of the Ḥaqīqah. The Exalted Lord first cleansed their hearts of whims and innovations. Then they could step onto the road of the Sunnah and find their way to the plain texts of Allah's Book and Muṣṭafā's Sunnah. In the verses about His attributes, they gave up their own imaginings and opinions and set aside their own cleverness. They bowed their necks in compliance, accepted what they heard, and took the road of surrender. So they escaped both likening Him to creation and stripping Him of His attributes.

Then He cleansed their hearts again, of this world and its stains. Then recognition lit up their hearts, and wisdom opened its eyes within them. He honoured them with His gaze and took love of the creatures out of their hearts, so they were wholly with Him. They went forward into solitude with Him and turned back from secondary causes to the Causer. They saw One, heard One and reached One. Their tongues were busy with remembrance, their hearts with reflection, and their spirits with love. Their tongues spoke of Him, their hearts whispered to Him in secret, and their spirits rejoiced.

As the verse says: "The moment my heart was captured by Your beauty, it became the slave of Your majestic loveliness. How exalted is the one who sees Your face, how great the one taken into Your keeping."

Know, though, that until the covenant from before time takes hold of your hem, your heart will not take up this work. Until the Real joins Himself to you, this path will not agree with you. Until the Real looks upon you, your heart will not long for Him.

"For what you used to do" is said to soothe the servant's heart and to add to Allah's tenderness toward him. The servant knows that his own careless deeds are not fit for that Threshold. He knows those stations and ranks are no payment for such deeds. Yet by His bounty Allah makes the unworthy worthy and adorns what is unlovely. In this He shows the servant the goodness of His lordship and His loving kindness.

### In short

- Before entering Paradise, the believers' hearts will be cleansed of every grudge, whether by settling rights or by a purifying drink.
- Rights left unpaid are settled in good deeds, so neglecting others' rights can leave a worshipper bankrupt.
- The people of Paradise will thank Allah, knowing they could never have been guided or done good without Him.
- Deeds are the occasion of Allah's mercy, but it is His mercy that admits a person to Paradise.
- Guidance has endless degrees, and entering Paradise is its final station.

44.text:
Once everyone has taken their place, a conversation takes place across the divide: "The residents of Paradise will call out to the residents of the Fire, “We have certainly found our Lord’s promise to be true. Have you too found your Lord’s promise to be true?” They will reply, “Yes, we have!” Then a caller will announce to both, “May Allah’s condemnation be upon the wrongdoers". The people of the Fire are addressed, rebuked and reproached once they are in their places.

### Phrase by phrase

**"The residents of Paradise will call out to the residents of the Fire"**: when all have entered their places, the people of Paradise will call to the people of the Fire. One explanation says they do it to affirm the truth, and another says to rebuke.

**"“We have certainly found our Lord’s promise to be true."** What our Lord promised us of Paradise, reward and favour has come true, for we have entered it.

**"Have you too found your Lord’s promise to be true?”"** O people of the Fire, have you found true the punishment and humiliation your Lord warned you of?

**"They will reply, “Yes, we have!”"** The disbelievers will admit that what they were promised about Hell has come true.

**"Then a caller will announce to both"**: a crier will proclaim between the two parties, making both hear.

**"“May Allah’s condemnation be upon the wrongdoers"**: the curse of Allah, His punishment, will rest on the wrongdoers, the disbelievers. They will be shut out of Allah's mercy. Its doors were open to them in their worldly life, and they turned away from them.

### How are the people of the Fire reproached?

Allah will punish the disbeliever for the claims he used to make in this life. In Sūrat aṣ-Ṣāffāt, Allah tells of a believer who had a disbelieving companion in the world:

> "Then he ˹and the others˺ will look and spot him in the midst of the Hellfire. He will ˹then˺ say, “By Allah! You nearly ruined me. Had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I ˹too˺ would have certainly been among those brought ˹to Hell˺.” ˹Then he will ask his fellow believers,˺ “Can you imagine that we will never die except our first death, nor be punished ˹like the others˺?”" (37:55-59).

The angels will also rebuke the disbelievers:

> "˹They will be told,˺ “This is the Fire which you used to deny. Is this magic, or do you not see? Burn in it! It is the same whether you endure ˹it˺ patiently or not. You are only rewarded for what you used to do.”" (52:14-16).

### A scene from Badr

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke in the same way to the dead thrown into the well at Badr. He called their leaders by name: "Abū Jahl ibn Hishām! ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah! Shaybah ibn Rabīʿah! Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true? I have found what my Lord promised me to be true." He meant that they had met the Fire, and he had been given victory. ʿUmar asked, "Messenger of Allah, are you speaking to people who have become rotting corpses?" He replied, swearing by the One in whose hand his soul was, "You do not hear what I am saying any better than they do, but they cannot answer."

### How could voices carry so far?

In earlier times people asked how this could be. Paradise is above the heavens and Hell at the lowest depth, so how could the voices of one reach the other? In this age of mass communication the question has become a matter of degree. People now know it is possible to see distant things and hear distant voices. What was unclear in ancient times has become easy to grasp through modern experience and observation.

This carries a lesson. If some statement of the Qur'an seems to defy explanation by today's knowledge, no conclusion should be drawn against it. As knowledge grows, it may well become an accepted fact tomorrow, however odd and unknowable it seems today. This does not mean the people of Paradise and Hell will talk by radio or television. It only shows that in Allah's universe there are arrangements that let two people far apart see and speak to each other without difficulty.

### In short

- The people of Paradise will call to the people of the Fire, affirming that Allah's promise came true, and the people of the Fire will have to admit the same.
- A caller will announce Allah's curse on the wrongdoers, who turned away from His mercy when its doors were open.
- At Badr the Prophet ﷺ addressed the dead leaders of Quraysh in the same words, and said they heard him.
- Something in the Qur'an that seems beyond explanation today should not be judged by present knowledge alone.

45.text:
The caller goes on to describe the wrongdoers on whom the curse falls: "those who hindered ˹others˺ from Allah’s Way, strived to make it ˹appear˺ crooked, and disbelieved in the Hereafter.”" Three crimes are named. They blocked others from the truth, they tried to distort it, and they denied the life to come.

### Phrase by phrase

**"those who hindered ˹others˺ from Allah’s Way"**: they turned away from Allah's religion themselves and turned others away from it too. They stood between people and Allah's path, meaning His law and the message of the prophets, and diverted them from His religion and from obeying Him.

**"strived to make it ˹appear˺ crooked"**: they wanted the path of truth to look twisted and winding, or changed, so that no one would follow it.

**"and disbelieved in the Hereafter.”"** They disbelieved in the meeting with Allah and in resurrection after death. They denied it would ever happen and neither accepted it nor prepared for it. That is why they made light of their evil words and deeds, since they feared no reckoning and no punishment. So they were, and are, the worst of people in word and deed.

### Why do some people see no force in the arguments for the Hereafter?

Only someone serious and sincere about an argument can feel how heavy it is. Those who give the Hereafter no importance cannot see the point of the arguments for it. Its reality is backed by very strong arguments, yet their unserious minds can only dig out faults in it. They raise objections of every kind. They fill themselves with suspicion and doubt, and they lead others into disbelief as well. In Allah's eyes such people are guilty in the extreme. They may think themselves entitled to His grace in this world, but in the Hereafter they will suffer His punishment.

However strong and convincing an argument is, clever talk can always cast doubt on it. Most people cannot tell a real argument from sophistry, so they drift away from the truth when they hear such talk. Some people are quite able to understand the truth and still drive others from it with clever words. On the Day of Reckoning, they will be far removed from Allah's grace.

### In short

- The cursed wrongdoers blocked others from Allah's way and tried to make the straight path look crooked.
- Their denial of the Hereafter made them careless of evil, since they expected no reckoning.
- Arguments for the Hereafter carry weight only for those who approach them seriously. Using clever talk to turn people from the truth is a grave crime.
